name: Crush: a sample-rate and bit reduction on every track, Rate on SWEEP and Bits on CONTOUR
description: The first effect of model27's Track FX (the filter slot of notes/72, which holds effects too since fltslot 0.7, notes/73), on any track whose sound chose it (RETRIG + PITCH), after Volume + Dist. RETRIG + SWEEP is Rate: off at the centre, the sample rate down to 1/64 of 48 kHz; to the right a hard hold (aliasing), to the left a soft one (the taken frames joined by lines). RETRIG + CONTOUR is Bits: off at 127, where a sound that steps to Crush starts (its start word, fltslot 0.8), then 8 bits and fewer to the left, one bit at 0 (since 0.4; 16 down to 1 before), without steps between (since 0.2; off at 0 in 0.1). Since 0.3 the same output in fewer instructions (the soft line's terms worked out when a frame is taken, the block scanned for silence only when the hold is silent). Both are real parameters of every machine: p-locks, LFO, velocity, CC 74 and 71. A note starts the rate's clock again. At Rate 0 and Bits 127 the track passes untouched, bit for bit.

uses.name: Crush
uses.why: an effect of the Track FX (the filter slot): called after Volume + Dist as (block, k 28 to k 31, track, triggered) on the tracks whose sound chose id 2

emulation.pattern: instructions per track and block, Crush's own code only, on the OS 1.13 in tools/emu/test_fltslot.py's filter_cost (mcengine.py's counter): all six tracks on it, the stock machines playing, a state held for 8 blocks after 8 of warm-up (off: Rate 0 and Bits 127; hard: Rate 48 with Bits 47; soft: Rate -48 with Bits 47; bits: Bits 47 alone; glide: Rate and Bits jumping every block, across the centre; silent: no note played, Rate and Bits on), the maximum, and the block in which the tracks come to it from none (its reset and first block); the filter slot's own instructions apart

unchanged: every track whose sound has not chosen Crush

emulation.tool: tools/emu/test_fltslot.py (Unicorn, the OS's own code; against the host build of the same source)
emulation.build: alone, with Samples and two references (four in one build)
